The load-bearing observation is the disagreement between the scan/discovery view (all zero) and the persisted pointer store (two indexed efforts) — with a genuine verdict-inverting reading: this may be the test's whole POINT (prove the session-lane scan reports n0 without leaking low-level seeded pointers into the count), in which case the 'inconsistency' is the invariant under test, not a bug. I name that disconfirmation and do not overclaim. The finding against that preference: committing a pointer that references an ignored-or-absent artifact turns 'durable history' into durable MISinformation — the split they are proud of is exactly what lets a committed pointer outlive and mis-describe its target. verdict: This is a healthy, correctly-scaffolded Anchor test fixture that faithfully reproduces an empty-lane 'OneSess' project — but it exhibits three real state-hygiene defects that would matter in production: pointer records that dangle to a nonexistent artifact, a placeholder 1970 timestamp seeded into a 'discovered' record, and a gandalf run record with no terminal-state reconciliation. The headline scan/store 'inconsistency' is most likely the intended invariant under test, not a bug.
